messages:
priya: FYI kicking off scoping for Q3: dedicated fallback lanes + SLA guarantees. Customers keep asking for predictable tail latency when burst consumes reserved capacity. Want to draft acceptance criteria, minimal failover playbook, and launch blockers.

lucas: quick q — do we intend regional failover, model downgrade, or token-throttling as the primary fallback?

ana: from enterprise calls: they'd prefer model downgrade + guaranteed max latency over dropped requests. Quality loss is acceptable if bounded.

miles: SRE perspective: we need a clear eviction order and backpressure model. soft-preempt vs hard-evict difference will shape rollout.

chris: idea: per-customer "grace credits" that permit bursts; when exhausted convert to reduced-perf mode. Need telemetry to detect abuse.

priya: proposal for acceptance criteria to start discussion: normal mode: 99.9% requests < 300ms; fallback guarantees 99.9% < 700ms with documented quality regression. Must include automated rollback and observable flags.

lucas: engineering knobs we should expose: `max_burst_tokens`, `grace_credits`, `fallback_model_map`, `preempt_policy`. Example config snippet: ```yaml
max_burst: 5m
grace_credits: 100
fallback: {redwood-mpt-7b: redwood-mpt-7b-quantized}
preempt: soft
```

miles: :thumbsup: playbook sketch: 1) mark tenant as DEGRADED 2) notify SE/cust 3) route to fallback pool 4) attempt scale-up of dedicated pool (if allowed) 5) billing adjustments + postmortem.

ana: launch blockers: confirm legal/data-residency for fallback models. Private/VPC customers may forbid routing to hosted fallback pools.

priya: good catch — add "data residency check" and explicit opt-out to launch criteria.

chris: suggested KPIs for acceptance: cost delta per 1k requests while in fallback, count of SLA breaches, sampled quality regression scores (human-eval on small prompt set). Also need alerting thresholds.

lucas: rough eng estimate: runtime changes ~3w, routing/policy ~2w, console + flags ~1w, integration/QA ~2w. Add a 1w buffer for security review.

priya: OK timeline — draft doc due next Tue; will include acceptance tests, alert recipes, and beta rollout plan.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created doc draft placeholder https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated-fallback-proposal

miles: I'll prepare an SLO appendix and a failure-mode simulation matrix to validate targets.

ana: I'll loop in AE for pilot customers (two accounts asked for predictable tail latency).

priya: thanks all — unless anyone objects to the latency targets above, I'll assemble the PR and post the spec for review Friday.
